examples.en: My father is a collector who gathers old coins.
The collector bought a rare stamp at a high price.

examples.ko: 저는 인형 수집가라서 집에 인형이 많아요.
examples.en: I'm a doll collector, so I have lots of dolls at home.
That collector's room is full of books.
The museum borrowed paintings from a collector.
Art collectors often visit exhibitions.

explain: 우표·동전·그림처럼 한 가지를 오래, 진지하게 모으는 사람에게 써요. 가볍게 모으는 사람은 그냥 '모으는 사람'이라고 해요. '우표 수집가'처럼 앞에 모으는 물건을 붙이고, 같은 뜻으로 '컬렉터'도 써요.

phrases.en: My grandfather is a famous stamp collector.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모으는 물건을 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the item being collected in front.

phrases.en: I went to an event where coin collectors gather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙여 여러 사람을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -들 to talk about several collectors.

phrases.example: 그 컬렉터는 그림을 백 점 넘게 가지고 있어요.
phrases.en: That collector owns over a hundred paintings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수집가'와 같은 뜻인데, 미술품이나 비싼 물건에 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수집가, but more common for art and valuable items.

explain_en: It is used for someone who seriously collects one kind of thing over a long time, such as stamps, coins or paintings. Someone who collects casually is just called '모으는 사람'. You put the collected item in front, as in '우표 수집가', and '컬렉터' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The church has about three hundred members.
Worshippers going to the temple line up.
He was a member of this church for a long time.
I'm worried because the number of members shrinks every year.
They say many new members have joined.
A representative of the members gave a speech.

explain: 같은 종교를 믿고 그 교회나 절에 다니는 사람을 가리켜요. 비슷한 '신자'도 많이 써요. '불교 신도', '교회 신도'처럼 종교나 장소 이름 앞에 붙여 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: This cathedral has many believers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신도'와 뜻이 거의 같아요. 특히 성당(가톨릭)에서는 '신자'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as '신도'; '신자' is used especially often for Catholic churches.

phrases.en: He was a member of the church for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소 이름 앞에 붙여서 어느 곳에 다니는 사람인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attaching a place name shows which place the person attends.

phrases.en: Buddhist followers gathered at the temple.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교 이름 앞에 붙여서 어떤 종교를 믿는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attaching a religion's name shows which religion the person follows.

explain_en: Refers to people who share a faith and attend a particular church or temple. The similar '신자' is also common. It can follow a religion or place name, as in '불교 신도' (Buddhist follower) or '교회 신도'.

en: all sorts of people; Tom, Dick and Harry; the rabble

examples.en: All sorts of random people gathered at that party.

examples.ko: 아무나 어중이떠중이를 다 뽑을 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't just hire any Tom, Dick or Harry.
That gathering is noisy because all kinds of people are there.

examples.ko: 어중이떠중이까지 다 나서니 일이 더 꼬였어요.
examples.en: With every Tom, Dick and Harry getting involved, things got even more tangled.
I'm not just some random person, I'm a real expert.

examples.ko: 어중이떠중이 말은 듣지 말고 직접 확인하세요.
examples.en: Don't listen to just anybody, check it yourself.

explain: 별 볼 일 없는 여러 사람을 한꺼번에 낮잡아 말할 때 써요. 사람을 낮추는 표현이라 상대방에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 돼요. 말하는 사람이 '내가 보기에 별로인 사람들'이라고 느낄 때 쓰는 말투예요.

phrases.en: A rabble of random people showed up and it was noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 사람을 낮잡아 한꺼번에 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 들 refers to a whole crowd in a belittling way.

phrases.en: Don't gather just any random people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자격을 따지지 않고 사람을 모을 때 비판하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A critical tone for gathering people without any standard.

phrases.en: Even every random person came, so there are no seats.
phrases.nuance_ko: '까지'를 붙여 별 볼 일 없는 사람들까지 모두 왔다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 까지 gives the sense that even the unremarkable people all came.

explain_en: It is used to look down on a crowd of ordinary or unimpressive people all at once. Because it belittles people, it is rude to use it directly about the person you are talking to. It reflects the speaker's feeling of 'people who don't impress me'.

examples.en: An elder of the academic world gave advice to juniors.
That actor is called a veteran of the film world.

examples.ko: 원로 가수의 공연에 많은 사람이 모였어요.
examples.en: Many people gathered for the veteran singer's concert.
I learned a lot listening to the elders' stories.

examples.ko: 우리 마을 원로께서 행사를 열어 주셨어요.
examples.en: An elder of our village held the event for us.
A veteran and a newcomer stood on stage together.

explain: '원로'는 한 분야에서 오래 일하고 존경받는 어른이에요. 보통 '원로 배우', '원로 가수', '원로 학자'처럼 직업 앞에 붙여요. 나이만 많은 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: A veteran actor received an award.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 활동하고 존경받는 배우를 높여 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful term for a long-active, esteemed actor.

phrases.en: An eminent senior scholar gave a lecture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학문 분야에서 오래 일한 존경받는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respected person with long years in academia.

phrases.en: I listened closely to the elder's advice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험이 많은 어른의 말을 존중할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to respect the words of an experienced elder.

explain_en: '원로' is a respected senior figure with a long career in a field. It is usually put before a job, as in '원로 배우' or '원로 학자'. It isn't used for someone who is merely old.

examples.ko: 몽골의 유목민은 양과 말을 키우며 살아요.
examples.en: Mongolian nomads live raising sheep and horses.
Nomads move with each season in search of grass.

examples.ko: 유목민의 전통 집인 게르를 직접 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have seen a ger, the traditional home of nomads, in person.
I saw a nomad family in the desert in a documentary.

examples.ko: 요즘은 노트북 하나로 일하는 디지털 유목민도 있어요.
examples.en: These days there are even digital nomads who work with just a laptop.
For nomads, a horse is the most precious property.

explain: 풀을 따라 가축을 키우며 옮겨 다니는 사람들에게 써요. 한 곳에 사는 사람은 '정착민', 농사짓는 사람은 '농경민'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 소리 나는 대로 [유몽민]이라고 읽는 것도 주의하세요.

phrases.example: 이 다큐멘터리는 유목민의 삶을 보여 줘요.
phrases.en: This documentary shows the life of nomads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '의'를 붙여 그 사람들의 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 의 lets you talk about the nomads' way of life.

phrases.example: 몽골은 오래전부터 유목 민족이 살던 곳이에요.
phrases.en: Mongolia is a place where nomadic peoples have lived since long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람보다 집단이나 민족을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a whole people or group rather than an individual.

phrases.en: Unlike nomads, settled people live in one place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한곳에 머물러 사는 사람을 뜻하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The contrasting word for people who live in one place.

explain_en: It is used for people who move around raising livestock and following grass. It helps to learn it with '정착민' (settlers) and '농경민' (farming people). Also note the pronunciation [유몽민].

examples.en: Medical professionals must protect patients' information.
Healthcare workers really went through a lot during COVID.
I went to the nursing department to become a medical professional.

examples.ko: 의료인에게 감사 편지를 쓴 학생이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many students wrote thank-you letters to healthcare workers.

examples.ko: 이 행사는 의료인만 참석할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only medical professionals can attend this event.

examples.ko: 의료인 부족 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The shortage of medical professionals often appears in the news.

explain: '의료인'은 의사, 간호사처럼 병원이나 의료 일을 하는 사람들을 크게 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 한 직업만 말할 때는 '의사', '간호사'처럼 구체적으로 불러요. 뉴스나 공문서에서는 '의료인', '의료진'이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The hospital's medical staff took good care of the patients.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의료인'과 비슷하지만 한 병원이나 팀의 사람들을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 의료인, but used more for the staff of one hospital or team.

phrases.en: I want to become a medical professional.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 진로를 말할 때 '되다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 되다 when talking about dreams or careers.

phrases.en: I sent thanks to the medical professionals.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 명을 말하고, 높일 때는 '께'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 들 makes it plural, and 께 is used to show respect.

explain_en: 의료인 is a broad word that groups doctors, nurses, and others who work in medicine. When you mean one job, you name it directly, such as 의사 or 간호사. The words 의료인 and 의료진 appear often in news and official documents.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 이민족의 침입을 막으려고 성을 쌓았어요.
examples.en: In the past, people built walls to stop invasions by other peoples.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 오랫동안 이민족에게 지배를 받았어요.
examples.en: That country was ruled by another people for a long time.
Living together with another ethnic group, the cultures blended.
People of other ethnic groups did business near the border.

examples.ko: 이민족을 차별하지 않는 사회를 만들어야 해요.
examples.en: We should build a society that doesn't discriminate against other ethnic groups.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 이민족이 세운 나라에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, I learned about a country founded by another people.

explain: 자기 민족과 다른 민족을 가리키는 말로, 역사나 뉴스 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 같은 민족은 '동족'이라고 하고, '이민자'는 다른 나라로 옮겨 사는 사람이라서 뜻이 달라요. '타민족'과 비슷하게 쓰지만 이민족이 조금 더 딱딱한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The walls were built to prepare for invasions by other peoples.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in historical contexts.

phrases.en: People of other ethnic groups live together in that country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷해요. 이민족은 역사 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning; 이민족 appears more often in historical contexts.

phrases.en: The general fought other peoples and protected the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '과'를 붙여 상대를 나타내는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the particle '과' to mark the opponent.

explain_en: It refers to a people different from your own ethnic group and mainly appears in history and news. People of the same ethnicity are '동족', and '이민자' means someone who moves to another country, so the meaning differs. It is used much like '타민족', though '이민족' feels a bit stiffer.

examples.en: A child should also be respected as an individual person.
Could a robot become a person with its own personality?

examples.ko: 부모는 자녀를 독립된 인격체로 대해야 해요.
examples.en: Parents should treat their children as independent individuals.

examples.ko: 그는 한 인격체로서 존중받고 싶다고 말했어요.
examples.en: He said he wanted to be respected as a person.
Many people treat their pets like persons.

examples.ko: 사람을 물건이 아니라 인격체로 보는 태도가 중요해요.
examples.en: It's important to see people as persons, not objects.

explain: '인격'은 사람의 됨됨이(인격이 훌륭하다)이고, '인격체'는 그런 인격을 가진 하나의 독립된 존재예요. '독립된 인격체', '인격체로 대하다'처럼 존중을 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: A child is an independent person, separate from the parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람을 따로 존중해야 하는 존재로 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used to say a person is a separate being deserving respect.

phrases.en: Please treat employees as individual people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 물건이 아니라 존중할 존재로 대한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means treating someone as a person to respect, not an object.

phrases.en: That teacher has an excellent character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 됨됨이를 말하는 말로, '인격체'보다 성품에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person's character, focusing on traits rather than being a person.

explain_en: '인격' is a person's character (as in '인격이 훌륭하다'), while '인격체' is the independent being who has that character. It is common in phrases about respect, like '독립된 인격체' and '인격체로 대하다'.

examples.ko: 그 단체의 조직원이 천 명이 넘어요.
examples.en: That group has more than a thousand members.
A notice went out saying they're recruiting new members.
The members meet every Monday.

examples.ko: 경찰이 범죄 조직원 세 명을 붙잡았어요.
examples.en: The police caught three members of a criminal organization.
The union first asked its members for their opinions.

examples.ko: 그는 조직원으로서 맡은 일을 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: As a member, he worked hard at the task he was given.

explain: 뉴스에서는 범죄 조직이나 정치 단체의 사람을 말할 때 많이 나와요. 회사나 모임 사람은 '직원', '회원', '구성원'이 자연스러워요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않는 편이에요.

phrases.en: The members gathered and held a meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 조직의 여러 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '들' refers to several members of the group.

phrases.example: 그 단체는 새 조직원을 모집하고 있어요.
phrases.en: That group is recruiting new members.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 새로 뽑을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when taking in new people.

phrases.en: The police caught a criminal organization member.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 흔하게 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in the news.

explain_en: In the news it mostly refers to people in a criminal or political organization. For people in a company or club, '직원', '회원', or '구성원' sound more natural. It is rarely used in everyday conversation.

dis.h: member of an organization, often criminal
gh: registered member of a club or site
someone who signed up for a service
formal term for a member of a meeting
a member making up a family or society

p.n: 조직원 sounds like a formal gang or organization member; 일원 is more neutral.

examples.ko: 검사 결과 그 아이는 두 사람의 친자로 확인됐어요.
examples.en: The test results confirmed that the child is the couple's biological child.

examples.ko: 친자 확인 소송 소식이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: News about a paternity suit came out on the news.
That child is not adopted but their biological child.

examples.ko: 친자와 양자를 차별하지 않는 부모도 많아요.
examples.en: Many parents don't treat their biological and adopted children differently.

examples.ko: 유전자 검사로 친자 여부를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can find out whether someone is a biological child through a DNA test.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 주인공이 친자가 아니라는 비밀이 밝혀져요.
examples.en: In the drama, the secret that the main character is not a biological child is revealed.

explain: 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 '친자 확인'처럼 자주 나오는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '친아들', '친딸', '친자식'처럼 말해요. 입양한 자녀는 '양자'라고 해서 짝으로 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: They did a paternity test at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in news and legal talk.

phrases.en: He is the boss's own son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '친자' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: What people say in daily conversation instead of 친자.

phrases.en: I am my father's own daughter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '친아들'의 짝으로, 피가 이어진 딸을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 친아들, meaning a biological daughter.

explain_en: This word often appears in news and legal contexts, as in '친자 확인' (paternity/parentage test). In everyday talk people say '친아들', '친딸' or '친자식'. It pairs with '양자' (adopted child), so it helps to learn them together.

examples.ko: 한국에서는 학연과 지연이 중요하다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: In Korea, people say school ties and hometown ties matter.
A rumor went around that he got promoted because of school ties.
We came from the same school, so we grew close through that tie.

examples.ko: 채용은 학연이 아니라 실력으로 해야 해요.
examples.en: Hiring should be based on ability, not school ties.
He worked without playing up his school connections.

examples.ko: 학연에 얽매이지 않는 회사를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a company that isn't bound by school ties.

explain: 같은 학교를 나와서 생기는 인연이에요. 한국에서는 '학연, 지연, 혈연'을 한 묶음으로 자주 말하고, '학연으로 뽑다'처럼 불공평하다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요. 좋은 뜻으로는 '동문', '선후배'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: This company doesn't care about school ties.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 학교 출신인지 보고 판단한다는 뜻이고, 보통 부정적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means judging people by which school they attended, usually negatively.

phrases.en: Hiring people through school ties is unfair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불공평한 일을 비판할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to criticize unfair practices.

phrases.example: 저는 그 회사에 학연이 없어서 소개받기 어려웠어요.
phrases.en: I have no school ties to that company, so it was hard to get an introduction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 학교 출신 인맥이 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you have no connections from the same school.

explain_en: It is the connection formed by attending the same school. Koreans often group '학연, 지연, 혈연' (school, hometown, family ties) together, and '학연으로 뽑다' carries a tone of criticism about unfairness. For a positive meaning, '동문' or '선후배' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 해병으로 군 생활을 했어요.
examples.en: My uncle served in the military as a marine.
The marine unit is near the coast.

examples.ko: 해병이 되려면 체력 시험을 통과해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a marine, you have to pass a fitness test.

examples.ko: 형이 해병에 지원해서 다음 달에 입대해요.
examples.en: My older brother applied to the marines and enlists next month.
The marines are training on the sand.
The marine in the movie looked really cool.

explain: 해병은 해군과 따로 있는 부대 사람이고, 바다에서 땅으로 올라가 싸우는 일을 맡아요. 군대 이야기에서는 '육군', '해군', '공군'과 함께 '해병대'라고도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My older brother joined the Marine Corps last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해병'은 사람이고 '해병대'는 그 사람들의 부대 전체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: '해병' is a person, while '해병대' is the whole corps they belong to.

phrases.en: He is a former marine, so he is strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 해병이었던 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who used to be a marine.

phrases.example: 저는 군대에 가면 해병이 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: If I go into the military, I want to become a marine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '되다'와 함께 써서 바라는 일이나 앞으로의 계획을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '되다' it expresses a wish or a future plan.

explain_en: 해병 is a member of the marine corps, which is separate from the navy and fights by landing from the sea. In talk about the military, people often say 해병대 (the Marine Corps) next to 육군, 해군, and 공군.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 혈연관계가 아니지만 친형제처럼 지내요.
examples.en: They aren't blood relatives, but they live like real brothers.
I heard they took a DNA test to confirm the blood relation.

examples.ko: 혈연관계가 없어도 가족이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can become a family even without blood ties.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 대부분 혈연관계로 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: Most people in this village are connected by blood ties.

examples.ko: 회사에서 혈연관계로 사람을 뽑으면 공정하지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't fair if a company hires people because of family ties.

examples.ko: 혈연관계보다 오래 함께 산 정이 더 중요할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes the bond from living together long matters more than blood relation.

explain: '혈연'은 피로 이어진 사이이고, '혈연관계'는 그 관계를 말해요. 같은 고향 사람끼리의 '지연', 같은 학교 출신끼리의 '학연'과 함께 '혈연·지연·학연'으로 묶어 말하는 경우가 많아요. 순우리말로는 '핏줄'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That person and I are not related by blood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '있다/없다'와 같이 써서 피가 이어졌는지를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'exist/not exist' to say whether there is a blood tie.

phrases.example: 혈연보다 친구가 더 가까울 때도 있어요.
phrases.en: Sometimes a friend is closer than a blood relative.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관계' 없이 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The short form without 'relationship'.

phrases.en: We look alike because we are of the same blood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순우리말이라서 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word that sounds softer in conversation.

explain_en: '혈연' is a tie by blood, and '혈연관계' is that relationship. It is often grouped as '혈연·지연·학연' with '지연' (ties from the same hometown) and '학연' (ties from the same school). The native Korean word is '핏줄'.

examples.en: Public officials must be honest.
My father worked as a public servant for a long time.
The assets of public officials were disclosed.
The newly appointed official gave a greeting.
Public officials may not accept gifts.
I study to become a public official.

explain: 나라나 지방 정부 일을 하는 사람을 두루 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '공무원'이라고 더 많이 말하고, '공직자'는 뉴스나 법에서 윤리나 책임을 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My uncle is a civil servant who works at city hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word used more often in daily life.

phrases.en: High-ranking public officials must disclose their assets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 자리에 있는 공직자를 말할 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news for officials in high positions.

phrases.en: Ethics for public officials are really important.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공직자가 지켜야 할 바른 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the proper conduct that officials must follow.

explain_en: It covers anyone doing work for the national or local government. Everyday speech prefers 공무원, while 공직자 appears in the news and in law when talking about ethics and responsibility.

examples.en: Teachers demanded protection of their authority.

examples.ko: 교권 침해 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Violations of teachers' rights often appear in the news.

examples.ko: 학생 인권과 교권이 모두 존중돼야 해요.
examples.en: Both students' rights and teachers' rights must be respected.
These days many people say teachers' authority has collapsed.
The school discussed ways to protect teachers' rights.

examples.ko: 교권 보호를 위한 법이 새로 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The law for protecting teachers' rights was newly revised.

explain: 학생의 권리를 말하는 '학생 인권'과 짝처럼 나오는 말로, 교사가 가르치는 일에서 존중받고 보호받을 권리를 뜻하는 쪽으로 많이 써요. '교권 침해', '교권 보호', '교권 추락'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 만나요.

phrases.en: You can report a violation of teachers' rights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교사의 권리가 해를 입는 일을 말하는 뉴스식 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase for harm done to teachers' rights.

phrases.en: The school gives education on protecting teachers' rights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교사가 존중받도록 지킨다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means protecting teachers so they are respected.

phrases.en: Students and parents should respect teachers' authority.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교사의 권위와 권리를 인정한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means acknowledging a teacher's authority and rights.

explain_en: It often pairs with '학생 인권' (students' rights) and mostly refers to a teacher's right to be respected and protected in their work. You often meet it in the news as '교권 침해' (violation), '교권 보호' (protection) and '교권 추락' (decline).
